p01.why: The call through the unknown reference s does not read the object, so it is a constant (Clang 18 rejects, Q-0090).

p02.why: later has only a declaration where v is initialized, and the later definition does not help.

p03.why: n is not const or constexpr, so it is not usable in constant expressions.

p04.why: A loop of 100000000 steps exceeds the step limits of all implementations in the matrix.

p06.why: A recursion depth of 400 is within the limits of all implementations in the matrix.

p07.why: bump changes counter, which existed before the evaluation.

p08.why: The throw is on a path that f(1) does not take.

p09.why: The goto is not reached by f(false).

p10.why: Constant evaluation must not convert a pointer to void to a pointer to an object type.

p11.why: A const int with a constant initializer is usable in constant expressions.

p12.why: n is const but its initializer is a call to a non-constexpr function, so it is not usable.

p13.why: Equality comparison of function pointers is allowed in constant evaluation.

p14.why: A constexpr pointer must not point to an object with automatic storage.

p15.why: Calls to lambdas are allowed in constant evaluation, and the lambdas are implicitly constexpr.

p16.why: A recursion depth of 100000 exceeds the limits of all implementations in the matrix.

p17.why: f reads u.i while u.f is the active member.

p18.why: The storage from new is never freed in the evaluation.

p19.why: A try block is allowed when no exception is thrown.

p20.why: The initializer of w is its own evaluation, which did not call f, so v is not usable there, and the error is diagnosed although f is never called.

p21.why: A const variable of enumeration type with a constant initializer is usable, so e + 1 is a valid array bound.

p24.why: f(1) divides by zero, which is undefined.

p25.why: The result points to storage that the evaluation allocated and did not free.

p26.why: Constant evaluation must not contain a reinterpret_cast.

p27.why: g reads through a pointer to x after f returned, which is a dangling read and undefined.

p28.why: The condition of explicit(...) must not narrow, and 2 to bool narrows (EDG accepts, Q-0078).

p29.why: f reads an object through a volatile lvalue.

p30.why: The variable of non-literal type is not reached by f(false).

p31.why: Storage from new[] is freed with delete.

p32.why: Both pointers refer to objects with static storage duration.

p33.why: Loops, calls and arithmetic on local objects are allowed; 1+4+9 is 14 and 16+1 is 17.

p34.why: The spec has no rule for non-type template arguments; by analogy with CE-11 the conversion of 300 to unsigned char narrows, so the guess is reject.

p35.why: The evaluation can change objects it created.

p37.why: A const volatile variable is not usable in constant expressions, so it cannot be an array bound.

p38.why: Each assignment makes that member active, so reading u.i after u.i = 9 is valid.

p39.why: n is constexpr, so n * 2 is a valid array bound and n a valid enumerator value.

p40.why: Each allocation is freed once with the matching form; 5 + 3 is 8.

p41.why: Comparing the addresses of two string literals is not allowed in constant evaluation; Clang rejects but GCC and EDG accept (Q-0033).

p43.why: f(false) does not reach the static variable.

p44.why: Constant evaluation must not order pointers to unrelated objects with <.

p45.why: Virtual calls to constexpr functions are allowed, and the call dispatches to Derived::id.

p46.why: A constexpr reference must not refer to a temporary object.
